$comment: Pinned, checksummed downloads for the bootstrap wizard. Generated from official release metadata on 2026-10-25; regenerate only with scripts/gen_pins.py. Every runtime download MUST verify against these digests.

linux-x86_64.name: qdrant-x86_64-unknown-linux-musl.tar.gz
linux-x86_64.$comment: musl build is statically linked — runs on every glibc (Debian 12 needs <= 2.36; the gnu build requires GLIBC_2.39 and aborts there). binary_sha256 verifies the UNPACKED engine after gzip extraction (the AppImage bundler corrupts ELF sidecars, so the engine ships gzip-compressed).

dehkhoda_dataset.$comment: nimah79/Dehkhoda-SQL pinned by immutable commit SHA; per-file sizes from the git tree (progress + sanity only; row-count USABLE_ROWS=312506 is the integrity check).

bm25_stats.$comment: v1.3.1 Option C: BM25 IDF statistics fitted ONCE on the deterministic first-30,000-row sample (ORDER BY id, meaning_clean — identical corpus to the monolithic DehkhodaLoader.ingest fit path) and pinned by sha256. The 5 CI shard jobs LOAD these stats (never refit) so cross-shard sparse ranking is consistent; the pre-job (scripts/build_bm25_stats.py) rebuilds and must match this pin or die fast. Cross-process byte-exactness proven twice locally (and the pickle re-built byte-identical after the sandbox reset).

prebuilt_index.$comment: v1.3.1 prebuilt Qdrant snapshot pin. The CI job build-index-snapshot generates the snapshot ONCE per release with the EXACT production ingestion pipeline, then verifies every field below. snapshot_sha256/snapshot_size_bytes/record_count are filled by the first successful CI run (small follow-up commit before the tag is pushed); later runs FAIL THE BUILD on any mismatch. Restoring requires the NATIVE qdrant sidecar in server mode — qdrant-client local mode does not support snapshots, so the full variant always launches qdrant_native first.
prebuilt_index.$comment_known_truncations: Chunks whose pre-embedding text exceeds the e5 model's 512-token max_seq_length (sentence_bert_config.json) and whose dense vector therefore covers only the first ~510 content tokens (sentence-transformers truncates silently). 384 of 351,156 chunks (0.109%) after the v1.3.1 chunker fix (else-branch hard-split, commit 'fix(chunker): hard-split oversized cur in the else branch'): all are <=1200 chars, worst 845 tokens — caused by vocalized Arabic vocabulary (harakat tokenize as separate XLM-R tokens, down to 0.71 chars/token), which the locked char-based chunking contract (chunk_chars=1200) cannot bound. NOT data loss: the BM25 sparse vector and the stored payload always cover the FULL chunk text, so lexical/RRF retrieval and displayed definitions are complete; only the dense side of these 384 chunks is partial. Token-aware chunking is the v1.3.2 follow-up.
prebuilt_index.$comment_record_count: record_count is the Qdrant collection points_count of the BUILT snapshot (filled by CI from the restored collection), NOT the source row count of the Dehkhoda SQL dump. Source-row integrity (USABLE_ROWS=312506) is asserted upstream in build-index-snapshot BEFORE the snapshot is created, so the snapshot is guaranteed to contain every usable row; the acceptance test then only verifies the snapshot restores fully (points_count == record_count).
prebuilt_index.$comment_source: Option A (run 41178302834 root cause): Qdrant snapshot containers embed a runtime collection UUID + timestamps, so re-merging identical shard data yields DIFFERENT archive bytes every run. snapshot_sha256 pins the EXACT BYTES we ship; convergence requires REUSE (actions/cache or the source_run artifact below), never REBUILD. Rebuild only on a real data change (model, chunker, corpus) = pin-bump event with a new r<N> cache key, not a retry.
